reason: Research (WebSearch plus a WebFetch of SEC EDGAR) shows the Brighthouse/Aquarian $70 cash deal still pending as of 2026-11-21. HSR, CFIUS and FINRA are cleared, but the Delaware, New York and Massachusetts insurance approvals are outstanding. The Q3 10-Q and the 11-05 earnings release say the approvals will not arrive by the Dec 6 outside date and that the parties are negotiating an extension and 'remain committed'. No amendment 8-K had been filed as of the last EDGAR listing (latest 8-K is 11-05), and AM Best still has BHF under review with negative implications. At the 40.84 mark the spread to $70 is about 71%. The market prices a low deal probability, and part of last week's ~9% slide was the SPY -8.6% beta drawdown rather than deal news. That leaves a sharply asymmetric hard catalyst inside two weeks: an extension announcement re-rates the spread, while a break probably gaps the stock toward standalone value in the mid-$30s. The existing -15% stop (about $38.11) and the 21% weight already cap that downside at roughly 3% of NAV before any gap, and the +45% TP (about $65) captures a close. Resizing or re-stopping would only add friction without improving that profile. The ~78% cash at 4% APY is deliberate, because I found no new hard catalyst worth deploying into during a five-day risk-off tape. The mandate is event-driven, not beta, so cash waits for the next defined catalyst.
